To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
glutathione reacts photochemically with thymine to produce 5‐S and/or 5‐S,S glutathione adduct.

irradiation of thymine or uracil in aqueous solution, in the presence of the tripeptide glutathione, produces 5‐S and 5, S‐cyclic glutathione‐5‐pyrimidine adducts, and the latter adducts can be reduced to the corresponding 5‐S or 5, S, S‐cycloadducts.
the photochemical reaction of glutathione with thymine and uracil in water produces 5‐S and 5‐SS‐substituted glutathione‐5‐pyrimidine adducts and 5‐cysteinely‐5‐pyridine adducts, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the photoreaction of thymine and uracil with the naturally occurring tripeptide glutathione in aqueous solution.
the photochemical addition of glutathione to uracil and thymine.
the photochemical addition of glutathione to uracil, thymine, and 5‐bromouracil.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the photoreaction of glutathione and thymine in the presence of sensitizers produces the glutathione adduct.
glutathione can react with pyrimidine bases in DNA to form 1‐ and/or 2‐cysteinyldihydropyridimines and 1‐cysteinedihydropyprimidines.
the photochemical addition of glutathione to uracil and thymine is a general process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
glutathione reacts with uracil and thymine to form 5‐S or S,S‐glutathionyl adducts.
the photoreduction of pyrimidines by glutathione is a two‐step process involving the formation of 5‐glutathionyloxy‐5, 5, 5‐triphenylhydantoin and the reduction of this intermediate by glutathione.
the photolysis of thymine‐ and uracil‐ glutathione adduct is a good model for the photoreactivity of the thymine and uracil residues in DNA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
glutathione is a good substrate for the photodriven synthesis of cysteine‐pyrimidine adducts.
glutathione can be a significant source of cysteine for DNA repair in cells.
glutathione is a very effective nucleophile for the photoreduction of pyrimidine bases in aqueous solution.
